 JUDGMENT This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 02-01-2024 at about 1.00 a.m., the petitioner was traveling as pillion rider on the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AL-3674, along with her husband, from 3rd Block Koramangala, 7th Cross, Wipro Junction towards BDA Junction, Bengaluru,
carefully, by observing vehicle movements on the said road.

At that time, the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-NM-3266 drove the same from 8th main road, Jai Puriya Junction towards 7 th Cross 8th Main Junction, in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner and her husband both fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over their body.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to St. John's Medical College Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.

sentences.text: Earlier to the accident she was working as a Senior Business Development Executive in Guvi Geek Network Private Limited, Chennai and earning a sum of Rs.58,300/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Adugodi Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.

The respondent No.1 is the owner and Apoorva vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190166016/

Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-, with interest at the rate of 24% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has contended that, at the time of alleged accident, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-AL-3674 was not holding valid driving licence to ride the said vehicle and he rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the insured car bearing No.KA-03-MN-3266 and caused the alleged accident.
The same is substantiated in the spot mahazar, spot sketch, drawn by the jurisdictional police.

The damages stated in the Motor Vehicle Accident report clearly goes to show that, there is gross negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-AL-3674.
Further it has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-NM-3266 vide policy bearing No.USGI/POSWEB/0821507/00/000 and its validity from 27- 05-2023 to 26-05-2024.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 02-01-2024 at about 1.00 a.m., near 8th main 7th Cross Junctin, 3rd Block, Koramangala, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-NM-3266 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.5, has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.

But, the respondent No.1 has failed to establish the said contentions.

In such circumstances, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that,

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-NM-3266 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle or there was any contributory negligence on his part,

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place in the junction of four roads, near 8th Main road - 7th Cross Junction, 3rd Block,
Koramangala, Bengaluru, in between the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-NM-3266 and motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AL-3674.

Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report,
which is marked as Ex.P.6, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AL-3674, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.5 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-NM- 3266 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

Admittedly, the said final report/charge- sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-NM- 3266.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 discharge summary, Ex.P.8 wound certificate,
Ex.P.16 case sheet, Ex.P.17 clinical note and Ex.P.18 x-ray, Ex.P.24 out- patient slip and Ex.P.25 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.

She has suffered right leg both bones (tibia and fibula) fracture, right hand 2nd metacarpal neck Apoorva vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190166016/

there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-NM-3266 and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained right leg both bones (tibia and fibula) fracture, right hand 2nd metacarpal neck fracture and left hand 4th proximal phalanx base fracture.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock,
loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

Further it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 02-01-2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 04-12-2025, which is after lapse of one year and eleven months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner,
duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.

Hence,
in the instant case the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

sentences.text: 31. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-03-NM-3266.

As per Ex.P.9 insurance policy, vide policy bearing No.USGI/POSWEB/0954786/00/000, issued by the respondent No.1, in respect of offending car bearing No.KA- 03-NM-3266, was valid from 27-05-2023 to 26-05-2024.

As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e.
02-01-2024.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.2.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-NM-3266 the accident in question has taken place.
